ai.title: Release script fetches version from npm registry
ai.summary: The release script now fetches the latest version from the npm registry instead of parsing GitHub release Atom feeds. This change replaces the fragile regex-based XML parsing of GitHub tags with a direct JSON request to `registry.npmjs.org`, ensuring version detection relies on the published package state. The update applies to the `npm-app/release/index.js` file.

eli5.text: The software that publishes new versions of the app now checks how others have already installed the product before, reading that information from a different, more reliable source instead of trying to interpret notes about past releases. This only affects the internal team that runs the publishing process, so anyone installing or using the product will not see this change. It is already live today.

ai.title: CLI input height scales to half terminal
ai.summary: Multiline input max height now `Math.floor(terminalHeight / 2)` in `cli/src/chat.tsx`. Replaces fixed `maxHeight: 5`. `useTerminalDimensions` exposes `terminalHeight` (default 24). Affects CLI chat rendering.

eli5.text: When typing a long message in the command-line chat, the text box now grows up to half the height of your terminal window instead of staying capped at a fixed five lines. If you open a larger terminal, the input area can expand further to show more of your message at once. This affects anyone using the command-line version of the assistant and is live today.

ai.title: Release 1.0.512 version bump for codebuff
ai.summary: Version string in npm-app/release/package.json incremented from 1.0.511 to 1.0.512 as a release-bump. This release bundles the same-day features: route subagent reasoning to agent streams with ancestorRunIds lineage tracking, add BYOK OpenRouter support with byok column in the message table, preserve pending agent responses on CLI cancellation, add GPT-5.1 code reviewer and editor variants to base2, thread AbortSignal through agent runtime and SDK run, and move CLI auth to full-screen app.tsx gating. Release script previously updated to fetch versions from npm registry [78f5fcd6].
ai.evidence: Diff in npm-app/release/package.json shows version field incremented from 1.0.511 to 1.0.512 for the codebuff package; this is a release-bump commit in sequence after the release script registry change [78f5fcd6] and before legacy release tooling update [f3d115f2].

ai.title: Release-legacy fetches latest version from npm registry
ai.summary: npm-app/release-legacy/index.js now fetches the latest legacy version from https://registry.npmjs.org/${packageName}/legacy instead of the GitHub releases.atom feed. This replaces the manual Atom XML regex parsing with direct JSON parsing of the registry response. The change is internal to the release tooling and does not affect the CLI or Web UI.

eli5.text: The internal release tool that prepares new editions of the legacy packages now looks up the latest version directly from the package registry's database instead of scraping a public release feed and guessing the version out of HTML tags. This does not change what you download or see in the app itself; it just makes the behind-the-scenes step of finding the right version faster and less error-prone. If you watched the build process, you would see it ask a different web address and parse a cleaner, structured response instead of pattern-matching text.

ai.title: Release-legacy package version bumped to 0.0.4-legacy.0
ai.summary: The legacy release channel package version in npm-app/release-legacy/package.json advanced from 0.0.3-legacy.0 to 0.0.4-legacy.0. This is a release-bump-only commit on the release-legacy surface; it increments the legacy channel version in lockstep with the main 0.0.4 release that shipped the earlier same-day user-visible CLI and web improvements. No source, CLI, or runtime files changed, the diff is limited to the version string in the legacy package manifest.
ai.evidence: In npm-app/release-legacy/package.json (release tooling), the "codebuff" package version field changed from "0.0.3-legacy.0" to "0.0.4-legacy.0", a one-character release bump in the legacy release channel, with no other files modified.

eli5.text: This release smooths out the login and setup experience for the command-line tool, making signing in and getting started feel more polished and full-screen. When you open the app, unauthenticated users now see a clean full-screen login prompt instead of a small pop-up window, and pressing Ctrl+C while signing in cleanly exits you back out. Links shown during login now hide the redundant http:// or https:// prefixes so your screen looks less cluttered while still pointing to the right place. After you log in or log out, the app properly clears your old session data and refreshes your connection so no stale credentials stick around between accounts. These changes make switching accounts, signing in fresh, and reading what is shown on your terminal feel faster and less error-prone every time you open the tool.

ai.title: Remove parentheticals from slash command labels
ai.summary: Slash command labels in `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts` no longer show redundant parentheticals. `logout`, `exit`, `usage`, and `new` commands now display their primary names only, as aliases handle secondary terms. This simplifies the CLI menu UI while preserving functionality via existing aliases.

eli5.text: When you open the CLI's help menu, the slash command labels now display only their primary name without parenthetical aliases. For example, instead of showing 'logout (signout)', it simply shows 'logout'. This affects anyone using the CLI's interactive commands. The redundant parentheticals were removed since the aliases still work through the existing shorthand system, making the menu cleaner and easier to read. This change is live today.

ai.title: Fix multiline input width calculation in CLI
ai.summary: Corrected width calculation for the CLI multiline input box by updating the dependency array in `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx`. The `useEffect` hook now includes `scrollBoxRef.current` alongside `width` to ensure accurate column measurement when the scroll box dimensions change. This resolves a bug where the input box incorrectly calculated its width as 1.

eli5.text: When you open the text input box in the command-line assistant, it now correctly calculates how wide it should be based on your terminal window. Previously, the box could shrink to a single character wide if the scrollable area's dimensions changed after the initial measurement. This only affects anyone typing long, multi-line prompts directly into the CLI tool.

ai.title: Remove unused slash-commands utility
ai.summary: Deleted `cli/src/utils/slash-commands.ts`. The `handleSlashCommands` function was unused in the current CLI architecture. This removes 133 lines of dead code related to local slash command interception (login, logout, exit).

eli5.text: The CLI tool removed a block of internal code that handled keyboard shortcuts like '/login', '/logout', and '/exit'. This code was no longer being used by the main program, so deleting it cleans things up without breaking any features you use. If you typed those commands now, nothing would happen differently than before, the removal only stripped out unused logic that had already been replaced. This is live today as behind-the-scenes cleanup with no visible effect on how the tool works.

ai.title: Suggestion menu compact layout for wide terminals
ai.summary: CLI suggestion menu switches to single-line layout when terminal width allows. Calculates max label/description lengths to determine fit, aligning descriptions with padding. Narrow terminals retain two-line layout with indented descriptions. Affects cli/src/components/suggestion-menu.tsx only.

eli5.text: When you open the list of suggestions in the command-line tool, it now tries to fit each suggestion and its help text on a single line if your terminal window is wide enough. If your window is narrow, it still falls back to showing the help text on a second, indented line. You would simply notice a tighter, single-row layout for each suggestion when you stretch your terminal wide, and no change when it's squeezed.

ai.title: CLI bootstrap comment
ai.summary: Added '// Hi!' comment to cli/src/index.tsx in bootstrapCli function. Internal code annotation only. No functional changes.

eli5.text: A developer left a small "// Hi!" note inside the program that launches the assistant window, sitting right above the code that draws the main interface. This is purely a behind-the-scenes marker: it does nothing, runs nowhere, and changes nothing about how the assistant opens, behaves, or looks, so you would not notice it in the app at all. Nothing you can see or use has changed as a result of this edit.

ai.title: Add decision-maker agent and base2-max-with-decision-maker
ai.summary: New `decision-maker` agent using `openai/gpt-5.1` added to resolve tricky implementation decisions. `createBase2` factory gains `withDecisionMaker` option, injecting the agent into the sub-agent list and prepending orchestration instructions to spawn it for key choices. A new `base2-max-with-decision-maker` orchestrator definition exposes this configuration. The `decision-maker` agent accepts a prompt and file paths, utilizing exploration and research tools to output a structured decision string.

eli5.text: The agent system now includes a new specialized assistant that uses an advanced model to help make tough implementation decisions, and the team can choose to activate it when orchestrating tasks. When enabled, this assistant is added to the team lineup alongside other specialists and receives extra instructions to consult it at key decision points. You would notice a new orchestrator option available today that includes this decision-making assistant, identifiable by its nickname 'Buffy the Max Decision Maker Orchestrator,' when selecting task configurations.

ai.title: Add providerOptions to agent definition for OpenRouter routing
ai.summary: Agent definitions now support `providerOptions` to control OpenRouter provider routing, fallbacks, and pricing caps. The `OpenRouterProviderOptions` type was refactored in `common/src/types/agent-template.ts` to separate reasoning and routing configurations. `packages/agent-runtime/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts` passes these options to the SDK, while `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts` applies them to provider requests. Dynamic agent schemas in `common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts` validate the new fields.

eli5.text: If you configure an agent to talk to OpenRouter, you can now tell it which AI companies to ask first, which to skip, and whether to let cheaper or different providers handle the request as a backup instead of just picking any available model. This gives you control over cost and which providers handle your requests, and it applies to agent setups that route through OpenRouter. The new settings are in place today and actively used when an agent is configured with provider routing options.

ai.title: Researcher-docs prompt simplified
ai.summary: Simplified instructions for researcher-docs agent. Enforces single read_docs call and ultra-concise reporting. Removes loop instruction. Affects .agents/researcher/researcher-docs.ts.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes helper that looks up documentation now uses a single lookup instead of repeating searches. As a result, its written summaries will be shorter and to the point. This is live today for anyone the internal agent serves.

ai.summary: Added cli/src/components/tools/read-docs.tsx for read_docs tool. Registers ReadDocsComponent in cli/src/components/tools/registry.ts. Renders compact bullet line showing libraryTitle and topic. No expand/collapse support.

eli5.text: When the assistant uses the built-in tool to look something up in a library's documentation, the command-line interface now draws a compact one-line entry for it instead of leaving it blank. You would see a single bullet line showing the library name and the topic it's reading about. This only covers displaying that summary line; there's no button to expand or collapse the details. The change is live today as part of version 1.0.512.
